issues.summary: Fix sequence lifelines and message signatures
issues.description:
Fix the lifeline names and message labels in the shared Visual Paradigm project.

Acceptance criteria:

* Use the same lifeline naming style across all sequence diagrams.
* Label requests and replies with their inputs or returned values, including asynchronous messages.
* Keep existing model IDs and unrelated diagrams unchanged.
* Save readable diagrams in the shared GitHub repository and publish the model to Visual Paradigm Teamwork.

The [model and previews are on main](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/tree/5c838de/docs/assignment-1-revision/interaction); the VP Teamwork commit is still pending.
Added four subtasks for lifeline names, message labels, model checks and publishing. The diagram edits and checks are complete. SCRUM-554 is still open until the model is published to Teamwork.

* Active risks name the next action and the task responsible for it.
* Keep comments short and save the updated register in the shared repository.

issues.description:
Agree on each team member's remaining work and availability.

Acceptance criteria:

* Record weekly availability and planned tasks through December 18.
* Name backups for code, data, diagrams and deployment, with any handoff needed.
* Record blockers, exams, absences and agreed scope changes.
* Review progress each week and adjust the plan with both members.

issues.summary: Verify clean-checkout setup and service recovery
issues.description:
Check that a clean checkout and the saved backups can restore a working development and demo setup.

Acceptance criteria:

* Follow the setup guide in a clean directory and record the commands, dependencies and disk space needed.
* Restore the pinned dataset and check its checksum. Keep the shot-data warning until the data is repaired.
* Document deployment and database recovery without sharing credentials.
* Record which recovery steps each team member has successfully checked.

issues.summary: Check deployment secrets and recovery access
issues.description:
Check that private credentials stay out of the app and shared files, and that the team can recover service access.

Acceptance criteria:

* Check tracked files and the built frontend for exposed private keys.
* Document required environment variable names, owners and recovery steps without their values.
* Test signed-out, expired-session and wrong-role access to protected routes.
* Confirm recovery contacts for GitHub, Google Cloud, Vercel, Supabase and Visual Paradigm.

issues.summary: Check hosting costs and prepare an affordable fallback
issues.description:
Keep the backend within the approved CAD10 monthly budget and prepare a fallback for demos.

Acceptance criteria:

* Record current charges by service separately from the forecast.
* Check the CAD10 alerts, CAD7 Cloud Run control and scale-to-zero settings. Account for delayed cost updates.
* If the forecast exceeds the budget, prepare a lower-cost setup or migration with backups and rollback steps.
* Verify sign-in and a recommendation on the chosen deployment and keep a usable fallback.

issues.summary: Document dataset sources and sharing permissions
issues.description:
Document where the Synergy and play-by-play data came from and how it can be used and shared.

Acceptance criteria:

* Record each source, retrieval method and applicable terms.
* Check permission for acquisition, hosting, reports and redistribution, including the assignment ZIP.
* Assign any unanswered permission questions for follow-up.
* Replace restricted data or remove it from distribution when permission is missing.

issues.summary: Review three coaching scenarios with a stakeholder
issues.description:
Review scouting, matchup preparation and a late-game decision with a stakeholder.

Acceptance criteria:

* Prepare the teams, game situation and task for each scenario.
* Record who reviewed it and whether they are a coach or a peer.
* Check whether they understand the recommendation, sample size and limits without help.
* Create tasks for the usability problems found and record unanswered questions.

issues.summary: Define evidence and cost checks for generated explanations
issues.description:
Plan an optional feature that explains the existing rankings. The current app uses fixed explanation templates.

Acceptance criteria:

* Give the feature the play IDs, evidence and numbers it may use; reject invented or conflicting details.
* Compare answers for accuracy and clarity, including repeated and unclear requests.
* Include a template fallback, timeout, cache, request limit and spending cutoff.
* Get separate provider and budget approval before enabling a paid model API.

issues.summary: Fix shot-team attribution and rebuild the shot dataset
issues.description:
The shot data has incorrect team labels: 18,746 rows list the same team and opponent, and all 7,520 games with at least 100 shots show only one shooting team. A TOR 2025-26 export also had 51 invalid rows out of 5,000.

To reproduce, run backend/tests/test_shot_attribution_regression.py with --runxfail and compare the TOR/BOS input events with the output team, opponent and home flag.

Acceptance criteria:

* Use explicit participant IDs to identify the shooting team. Changing a score must not change the team.
* Recover the original event data and rebuild the cleaned dataset and derived files.
* Pass the row and game checks and compare samples with the original events before relying on shot results.

comments.body: Added four tests for incorrect shot-team labels: two small TOR/BOS examples and two checks of the saved dataset. All four still fail when run with `--runxfail`, so the data repair is still needed. The [tests are on main](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/9804b32ca45ce9f21763cc027cf75e8f30d397aa), and [CI passed with these marked as known failures](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/actions/runs/38173001625).

issues.summary: Use the new Gameplan situation on the first Build
issues.description:
The first Gameplan Build uses the previous game situation. Clicking Build again uses the new values and changes the rankings.

To reproduce, start with TOR/BOS 2024-25, Q4, 180 seconds and margin -2. Enter "Q4 down 5 with 0:28 left", then click Build twice without changing anything.

Acceptance criteria:

* The first request and the page both use period 4, 28 seconds and margin -5.
* Pass the parsed situation directly into the ranking request.
* Add a test showing that unchanged inputs give the first and second builds the same context.

issues.summary: Pass supported coaching conditions into Gameplan ranking
issues.description:
Gameplan recognizes phrases such as "Need a three" and "They are switching", but only sends numeric context to the ranking API.

To reproduce, enter those conditions and compare the parsed values with the request built by GameplanClient.

Acceptance criteria:

* Define which coaching conditions the ranker supports.
* Send supported conditions to the API and test their effect.
* Clearly show when a condition is unsupported and does not affect the ranking.

issues.summary: Preserve overtime in the Gameplan context
issues.description:
Gameplan changes overtime to quarter 4 before ranking.

To reproduce, enter an overtime situation, build the plan and compare the parser result with the displayed period and ranking request.

Acceptance criteria:

* Keep the overtime period through parsing, display and ranking.
* Validate the overtime clock without changing the period.
* Add a test covering the complete parser-to-ranker path.

issues.summary: Clear Model Metrics loading state when requests finish
issues.description:
Model Metrics keeps showing "Loading pipeline summary" and disables Refresh even after the holdout results appear.

To reproduce, sign in as an analyst, open Model Metrics and wait for the results table. The recorded run displayed Ridge RMSE 0.011 while the loading message remained.

Acceptance criteria:

* Track the summary and evaluation requests separately.
* Clear loading on success or error and allow a retry.
* Avoid duplicate initial requests and test loading, success and failure states.

issues.summary: Load saved shot metrics without training during page requests
issues.description:
The default Shot Model Metrics request timed out after 300 seconds with HTTP 504 in the October 6 run. It has not been repeated during this revision.

Use the saved request and runtime results to investigate. After the fix, open the page once and record its result and response time.

Acceptance criteria:

* Load saved or precomputed metrics during normal page visits.
* Run expensive evaluation in a separate bounded job or preparation step.
* Show useful loading and error messages, and complete supported requests before the platform timeout.

issues.summary: Align analyst shot pages with their API permissions
issues.description:
Analysts can open Shot Plan and Shot Heatmap, but their requests use coach-only APIs and return HTTP 403.

To reproduce, sign in as an analyst and run either page with a supported season and matchup.

Acceptance criteria:

* Decide which roles should use each page.
* Make navigation, page access and API permissions agree.
* Test allowed, wrong-role and signed-out access without opening unrelated coach-only routes.

issues.summary: Render Shot Statistical Analysis using the current API fields
issues.description:
Shot Statistical Analysis receives a successful API response, then crashes while reading dropped.length. The response uses removed, and other page sections also expect older fields.

To reproduce, run the analysis as an analyst and compare the response with the fields used by the page.

Acceptance criteria:

* Update the types, response adapter and page components to match the API.
* Handle missing optional sections with an accurate unavailable message.
* Add a render test using a current response. Do not show results the API did not calculate.

issues.summary: State when baseline explanations do not use game context
issues.description:
Baseline explanations do not say that score, period and clock were left out. BST-99 found this in all five returned explanations.

To reproduce, request baseline Top-K for 2024-25, TOR against BOS, K=5 without game context.

Acceptance criteria:

* Say when game context was not used.
* Keep context-based explanations tied to the values actually used.
* Rerun BST-97, BST-98 and BST-99 against the corrected code and deployment.

issues.summary: Define backend readiness and explain missing prerequisites
issues.description:
A missing Synergy file produces a traceback. Missing Supabase settings still allow startup and /health 200, although protected requests remain blocked. The tests and app need a clear agreement on what "ready" means.

Acceptance criteria:

* Define startup requirements and separate running from ready to serve requests.
* Report missing data or auth settings clearly without exposing secrets.
* Do not report production readiness when required settings or data are absent.
* Keep development and isolated tests supported, then update and rerun BST-107 and BST-113.

issues.summary: Report unmapped shot-data columns during schema validation
issues.description:
BST-116 reports the missing TEAM_ABBR column but says nothing about an unused UNMAPPED_FIXTURE column. Extra metadata is allowed and is already excluded from model features.

Acceptance criteria:

* Report mapped, optional, ignored or unmapped, and missing required columns.
* Identify unused metadata without treating every extra column as an error.
* Keep missing-column errors clear and rerun both BST-116 examples.

issues.summary: Validate shot margins and define when prediction inputs are available
issues.description:
All 1,332,515 retained shot rows have no MARGIN value, but model loading replaces it with zero. The app also needs to explain whether it predicts before a possession or evaluates a proposed shot.

Acceptance criteria:

* Recover real margins or show them as unavailable instead of treating missing values as tied scores.
* State when each prediction input becomes available.
* Use only prior information for pre-possession predictions. Define a separate input contract for a proposed-shot evaluation.
* After SCRUM-538 repairs the source data, rerun BST-117, BST-118 and BST-119 with finite-feature checks and later-season, per-fold results.

Related work: SCRUM-526.

issues.summary: Set and verify the deployed Top-K response-time target
issues.description:
BST-111 needs an agreed response-time target. All eight test requests succeeded, but two took about 33 seconds with four running at once.

Acceptance criteria:

* Agree on a Top-K timing target, including cold starts and concurrent requests.
* Investigate slow requests using a limited test run and service logs.
* Rerun BST-111 and record the environment, sample size, target and p95 response time.
* Stay within the approved hosting budget.
